findings.where: design C.2, C.3, D9, OQ-3, RA-10
findings.problem: AC 13 (and 0051 D9/Q3) require a user to hold a TASK_WORKER grant whose subtree covers the task's scope node. The design builds, by DEFAULT, the union of all roles whose permission allows the route (f1_allowed? calls Scope.allowed?(principal, route_permission, {:node, id})). TasksComplete/TasksRead are also held by PROCESS_OPERATOR and TENANT_ADMIN, so a user with a scoped PROCESS_OPERATOR row on the node, plus routing role membership, would pass F1 although AC 13 says TASK_WORKER. The wider reading is built before REQ-ANALYST rules (OQ-3 open) and the fail-closed rule says the narrow reading is the default. f1_allowed?(task, principal, permission) cannot express the literal rule at all.
findings.required_change: Make the AC-literal rule the build default for see/claim/complete (TASK_WORKER effective scope over {:node, id}): specify the exact function that evaluates one named role's scope against a resource scope (signature, deny shape, NULL node :unresolvable, token principal, PLATFORM_ADMIN handling, tenant-wide TASK_WORKER) and use it in Tasks.f1_allowed?/3, Tasks.in_scope/3's set (allowed_set for the TASK_WORKER role, not for the route permission) and the list/get predicate. State explicitly that assign/reassign (not in AC 13) use the route permission, and why. Keep the wider reading only as OQ-3 with the amendment RA-10 pending, not as the built default. Update T-F3..T-F7 with a scoped PROCESS_OPERATOR-only negative case.

findings.where: design F3, 3.2, OQ-1, OQ-4, R-3, residual R-7
findings.problem: Allowing a ScopeDeclaration on an UNMANAGED module-shipped type removes the protection 0051 D6/M4 relies on (managed-type lock) while the definitions API still lets a PROCESS_DESIGNER create, supersede or activate a tenant type of the same name (OQ-4 is deferred as 'no AC'). R-7 says this is 'restrictive only'; that is false for a :tenant_wide declaration: a tenant-defined or superseded type carrying that name is then readable by every scoped caller that passes the coarse check (T16), which is the self-service exemption M4 forbids. SEC ruling R-3 as stated ('IN; alternative makes AC 6-9 untestable') hides this.
findings.required_change: Choose and specify one: (a) OQ-4 refusal in 518 (definitions API refuses create/activate/supersede of a type name declared by any installed module's :scope_declarations, with a route-level test and the same constant-403 shape as managed types), or (b) restrict declarations on unmanaged types to non-production modules (Catalog rule 11 rejects :scope_declarations for a type not in the same manifest's :manages_entity_types unless the module id is in a test-support allowlist set by config only in the test env), so the pilot state remains exactly 'nothing declared in production' and the hole cannot exist until OQ-4 is built. Correct R-7 and the R-3 question text accordingly, and restate R-3 so SEC rules on the actual risk.

findings.problem: 2c-i carries ACs 1-5, 18, 21 and 23: compiler arity change and 9 call sites plus 67 forced test edits, ScopeDeclaration with manifest key, Catalog rule, ManifestHash, Scope.allowed_set, ScopeNodePaths.allowed_node_ids, join ON predicates, ScopeGate, the Enforce before-send backstop, RouteScope flips and six new walk errors, the self-service list and walk, the fixture module, ~35 tests and the exam fallback (about 20 signatures if R-1 is not ruled in, which is now the build default). That is not one agent turn. 2c-ii (ScopedLookup, ScopedWrites, Records scope_check, import pre-check, 4 attachment routes, 8 resolvers, walk rules) is large but coherent; 2d (migration, Tasks, Engine in-transaction recheck, docs, 7 routes) is borderline once G1 is reworked.
findings.required_change: Split 2c-i into two ELIXIR-DEV turns/PRs with a stated boundary, e.g. 2c-i-a = compiler arity + 9 sites + forced test edits + allowed_node_ids + allowed_set + ScopeDeclaration/manifest/Catalog/ManifestHash + fixture module (ACs 1-5, mutants M1-M11) with NO route reclassified, and 2c-i-b = ScopeGate + Enforce backstop + RouteScope flips/walk + 3 :filter routes + self-service (ACs 18, 21, 23). Update section 1 table, section 9 AC map and 3.1 file map; state which PR owns the exam threading. Give 2d an explicit internal commit order (migration + fixture, Tasks reads, router gates, Engine recheck, docs) and say the turn may be split at the Engine recheck if it exceeds one turn.

findings.problem: 'Scope-404s are counted in telemetry, NOT audited.' The design says telemetry carries counts only (12.1) but defines no event for a scope refusal on the data path.
findings.required_change: Either name the event (for example [:letflow, :scope, :refused] with measurements %{count: 1} and metadata policy key and class only, no ids) in ScopeGate/ScopedLookup/Tasks.in_scope, with one test, or state in section 12 that it is deferred to REQ-519 with the reason.

findings.problem: 'continues into the branch the nonexistent parent takes today' is ambiguous for create: today a nonexistent parent with no file part answers 422, with an oversized file 413. The designed behavior is that BOTH out-of-scope and nonexistent parent short-circuit to 404 for a scoped caller (equal to each other, which is what AC 11 asks); the sentence should say so. Mutant ids M1-M35 also collide with ledger ids M1/M2 and 0051 M2/M5.
findings.required_change: Reword 5.5: for a scoped caller both cases take the same short-circuit (404 on create/get/delete, empty page on list) before any multipart read; rename the mutants X-1..X-35 or the ledger rows.

findings.problem: The before-send backstop turns a 2xx into a 500 AFTER a resolver-route write may have committed. It fails closed for the response but not for the write. It is design-added hardening (not in AC 23); acceptable if SEC rules it IN with that stated.
findings.required_change: State this limit in OQ-8 so SEC rules on the actual property.
